label: Delegation metaphor
summary: The delegation metaphor is an alternative framing for human-AI interaction, proposed as a better fit than conversation for agentic AI use cases. It describes a pattern where a human hands off a request, a set of agents processes it out of sight, and a deliverable is returned. Unlike conversation, it does not imply turn-taking, equal exchange, or anthropomorphism.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike introduces delegation as a metaphor specifically to address the limits of 'conversation' when describing agentic AI workflows. Where conversation implies mutual stakes, trust contracts, and back-and-forth exchange, delegation better captures what actually happens: you submit a request through a mix of language and GUI inputs, a swarm of agents works on it without your involvement, and you receive an end result. She flags this metaphor as the better fit for agentic AI rather than as a universal replacement for all GenAI interaction patterns.
open_questions: The passage on delegation is cut off mid-sentence, so it is unclear what full implications or caveats Maaike intended to draw out.
If delegation replaces conversation as the dominant metaphor for agentic AI, what design consequences follow for how interfaces should handle the waiting period when agents are running?
